set.st: French trader Joseph Bertrand, founder of Bertrand (4 mi S of Niles), sold land and buried "a full bushel of gold and silver coins" from fear of robbers, then forgot the spot; he believed it was under an apple tree in his orchard. Hundreds searched; "every foot of the orchard" was dug by 1898-99. Pin is between his 1873 house lot and estate, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Bertrand village site, Bertrand Twp. 1873 village plan: his house lot in the village and 52-acre estate inside the river bend to the south; village gone by 1887.
set.t: The village is gone; Michigan marker S0286 (Bertrand Rd at Bond). The 1898 search was in his old orchard, probably on the house lot or the estate land; check both on the 1938 aerial. Wire story, one origin: second source wanted (Berrien county history 1880). Access: private farmland: permission.
pinev: Parcel-level: the 1873 Berrien atlas "Plan of Bertrand" shows his house lot in the village on the N bank of the St. Joseph River bend and his 52-acre estate on the riverside land inside the bend just S of the village; pin between them (about 450 m).
